what_went_wrong: Agent correctly found sanitize.js only had validateFeedback at this point, then reasoned new comment validation 'could be added inline elsewhere' without touching sanitize.js. The actual commit extended this exact file with a new validateComment rule set, following the established validator-file pattern the agent itself had just observed. Agent flagged its own confidence as LOW, showing awareness of the uncertainty.

Agent found that edit/detail/order endpoints already work against the current schema and concluded no schema change was needed. The actual commit added new pre-order and size-specification sub-schemas to support richer detail/order views -- a forward-looking schema extension the agent had no way to anticipate from present functionality alone.

Classic same-topic-different-file default: agent found getPosts() has no location/blood-type filter and inferred the controller must change. The actual implementation added filtering entirely in a separate service file (bloodNotificationTransformer.js) and the frontend, never touching marketplaceController.js. This exact failure pattern was also the single most persistent false activation in the original Conditions A/B/C on this dataset.

Agent correctly determined NotificationTray.jsx did not exist yet and correctly predicted a new component would be built at roughly that role/location, but classified 'the file will be created' as NOT_APPLICABLE to a 'do not modify' constraint. The benchmark's ground truth treats file creation at the constrained path as APPLICABLE. This is a genuine semantic disagreement about whether creating a file counts as 'modifying' it, not a factual investigation miss.

Agent correctly found no donor/blood-request logic in auth.controller.js. Ground truth explains the actual commit also incidentally commented out an unrelated email-domain check in googleSignin as part of the same commit -- a bundled, task-unrelated edit with no trace inferable from the task description or the pre-commit repository state.

Agent classified RoommateCard.jsx as a passive read-only display component and assumed the task's 'listing forms' language pointed only to PostRoommateForm.jsx. The actual commit substantially changed RoommateCard.jsx (97 lines) to reflect updated listing data/UI -- a page/component conflation similar to the Dashboard/LiveFeed pattern noted in the original A/B/C report.

Agent correctly found no Notification.js file and correctly noted the app's primary data layer is Prisma, but over-generalized this into 'the app doesn't use Mongoose models here' and concluded no such file would be created. In the same commit, the sibling case (22) showed notification.controller.js was an empty stub about to be built out -- the agent flagged that controller as APPLICABLE but did not connect it to a matching new Mongoose model being created alongside it for the same feature.

Agent correctly identified ChatbotWidget.jsx as pure UI and the RAG search/ranking logic as backend-only, reasoning query preprocessing/reranking belong in search.py. Ground truth confirms the backend reranker/preprocessor modules were the primary change but notes the commit ALSO substantially changed ChatbotWidget.jsx (228 lines) alongside them -- a bundled UI change not implied by the task wording ('using query preprocessing and a reranking step').

Agent found getMe/updateUserProfile already exist and reasoned the profile page could be built by consuming them unmodified. The actual commit extended auth.controller.js itself (22 lines) alongside the new Profile.jsx page -- an 'existing endpoint looks sufficient' assumption that missed the endpoints were being extended to support the fuller profile page, not just consumed as-is.
